messages:
Priya Shah: FYI — internal request to onboard model 'monoceros-14b' from Search infra. They want it as a reranker replacement. Attached: weights tar, tokenizer, minimal README. Priority: medium-high, customer wants p95 <50ms on 512-tokens.
Ethan Lee: sending links? do we have HF id or just tarball? any license issues?
Priya Shah: tarball only, license is CC-BY-NC (customer confirmed). HF id not provided. They included a model_card.md.
Marta Gómez: quick checklist: tokenizer check, model config (vocab_size, hidden_size), kv-cache layout, dtype (fp16?), and whether it uses rotary embeddings. I'll grab the tar and run tokenization smoke tests.
Ethan Lee: if fp16 we should try 4-bit/8-bit quant profiles later. For first pass: run an unoptimized smoke run to confirm logits and shape sanity.
Samir Patel: I'll take perf bench (short sequences). Plan: spin a small job on the dev-gpu pool, run 1000 inferences with batch sizes [1,4,8], measure p50/p95. Will post script.
Priya Shah: customer provided benchmark numbers: current p95 ~140ms on their setup (A10g). They expect us to get <=50ms after infra tuning. Not sure if that's realistic but worth attempting.
QuantBot: Automated scan: model has 14 layers, attention heads=16, rotary embeddings present, kv_cache_enable=true. Size ~28GB fp16. Potential quant targets: awq-4-g, ngq8.
Marta Gómez: noted. tokenizer passes sample text, encodes/decodes stable. model forward returns logits shape [1,512,vocab]. no NaNs.
Ethan Lee: run this first command to smoke run on a dev GPU:```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
import torch

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('/tmp/monoceros-14b')
model = torch.load('/tmp/monoceros-14b/model.pt')
inputs = tok('test query', return_tensors='pt')
with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(**inputs)
print(out.logits.shape)
```
Samir Patel: posted preliminary perf (dev-gpu small): batch1 p95=120ms, batch4 p95=85ms, batch8 p95=92ms. So baseline's worse than target. I'll try kernel/autotune flags and a 4-bit AWQ run.
Marta Gómez: also ran small eval set (50 queries) against current in-prod reranker. metric: MRR. monoceros MRR=0.78 vs prod 0.80 — small quality regression. Need to capture which prompt families regress.
Priya Shah: that's important. Customer will tolerate small perf drop if latency gains and cost improve, but we need to surface regressions. Can we run per-slice analysis?
Ethan Lee: yes — set up eval harness with the rerank testset. Run full 2k queries, compute MRR by slice (query length, domain). I'll queue it.
QuantBot: Suggestion: run AWQ-4-g and ngq8 experiments and compute delta MRR. Also run temperature-stable prompts.
Samir Patel: did awq-4-g quick pass: quantized model size ~9GB. Inference batch1 p95 ~55ms on same dev-gpu with kernel-opts. Quality: MRR drop to 0.76 overall; some long-tail queries drop more.
Marta Gómez: can we try cacheable prefix optimization and batching tweak? For rerank workload, typical context is short; enable continuous batching and set max_batch_latency=20ms.
Ethan Lee: propose rollout plan: 1) complete full eval (2k queries) for FP16 baseline, AWQ-4, NG8; 2) decide acceptable MRR delta (customer prefers <=0.03); 3) if meets, create canary route on dedicated pool with 5% traffic; 4) monitor MRR, latencies, errors for 24h.
Priya Shah: agreed. I'll coordinate with Search infra to define SLA and acceptable delta. Also need privacy review because customer data used for eval.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deployment job created: job_id=canary-2627654321-1. Will wait for approval from @Priya Shah and @Samir Patel.
Samir Patel: I'll approve once full eval is in. ETA 6-8 hrs to get bench + quant experiments completed.
Marta Gómez: I'll attach the per-slice CSV and failing examples to the intake doc so product/CS can triage with the customer.
Ethan Lee: one more: tokenizer vocab has a few OOVs for domain tokens; recommend adding a small custom tokens patch to reduce spoofing and improve MRR.
Priya Shah: noted — adding to action items. Thanks all. I'll update customer and set expectation for next status in ~8h. :thumbsup:
